And because of this, flatterers were calling him a god.
And because he did not rebuke them, he was consumed by a plague,
and after five days he perished.
After Gaius Caesar, Claudius Caesar [ruled] fourteen years.
In his time there was a disturbance in Jerusalem on the day of the feast of Passover.
And as the people were crushed at the exits of the Temple,
thirty thousand Jews were trampled on by one another and died.
And there was a great famine throughout the whole inhabited world,
and the prophecy of Agabus which is in the book of Acts was fulfilled.
And the disciples in Antioch, as much as they were able, set aside and sent to the poor who were in Jerusalem.
And Philo the wise met the apostle Peter while he was preaching in Rome,
and he wrote concerning those who were being discipled to the faith in our Lord,
that they were stripped of possessions and of the care of the world,
and that none of them would taste food before the sun set,
judging that the work of wisdom is like light,
and bodily need is like darkness.
And there are some who do (not) eat for two days,
and some for three,
and others for six or seven.
At this time, an Egyptian man, a false prophet, came to Judea,
and led astray after him thirty thousand people.
And when he led them about in the wilderness,
he brought them to the Mount of Olives,
wishing to capture Jerusalem.
Then Felix arrived,
and a battle took place.
And the Egyptian fled,
and his army perished.
And concerning this it was said to Paul by the chiliarch:
"Are you not then that Egyptian?" and so forth.
After Claudius Caesar, Nero Caesar [ruled] fourteen years.
He sent Festus and dismissed Felix.
And he was the first to raise a persecution against the Christians,
in which Peter and Paul bore witness and were crowned in Rome.
And in the thirteenth year of Nero, the Jews rebelled.
And Nero sent Vespasian and Titus his son.
And in that same year, on the first of Hazīrān, Titus captured the city of Jotapata,
because he heard that Josephus the historian, the son of Matthias the priest, was there,
who was the commander of the army of the Jews.
